samples.summary: The new `workflow_run.path` gate in agent-iterate-ci.yml has no test at all
samples.evidence: The diff adds `github.event.workflow_run.path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'` to the `gate` job of agent-iterate-ci.yml — the arm that drives a `contents: write` fixer. checks.test.mjs pins the equivalent clause only for agent-review-panel.yml (the gate/concurrency evaluator at checks.test.mjs:169-218 reads `^ {2}gate:` out of `agent-review-panel.yml` and nothing else). I grepped scripts/ for `workflow_run.path` (only checks.mjs and checks.test.mjs's panel test match) and for `agent-iterate-ci` (only loop-status.test.mjs's CI_PAGED_LATCH string test and comments in agent-workflow-guards.test.mjs). Deleting the new clause from agent-iterate-ci.yml leaves every suite green, so this guard can be regressed silently — the same class of silent-skip the change's own comments say must never happen.

samples.summary: The new `workflow_run.path` clause in ci-report.yml is untested; nothing pins the job's `if:`
samples.evidence: ci-report.yml's job `if:` is rewritten to add `github.event.workflow_run.path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'`. scripts/test/ci-workflow.test.mjs contains many ci-report.yml assertions (inline glob matcher, token scoping, step requires, GATE_STEP, comment interpolation) but none extract or evaluate the job's `if:` expression — I read the match list for `ci-report` across scripts/ and none of the hits touch the trigger gate. So the clause (and the `event == 'pull_request'` clause it now folds into a `>-` block) can be dropped or mis-edited with no failing test, on the one path the diff's own comment says fires on PR branches where forgery is not merge-gated.

samples.summary: "the copies agree" test compares checks.mjs against a re-implementation inside the test, not against the workflow YAML
samples.evidence: checks.test.mjs:596-616 declares `const inline = (runs) => {...}` — a hand copy pasted into the test file — and then asserts `ciRunToRerun(fixture)` equals `inline(fixture)` for six fixtures. That loop can never fail because of anything in agent-loop.yml or agent-rerun.yml; it compares checks.mjs to the test's own copy. The only real link to the YAML is three regexes (`r\.status === 'completed'`, `r\.id > n\.id`, the `if (run) { await ... reRunWorkflow` shape) over a fixed `yml.slice(at - 200, at + 700)` window. Concretely: reverting the diff's `github.paginate(..., per_page: 100)` back to `listWorkflowRuns({... per_page: 1})` keeps every one of those regexes matching (the filter/reduce lines are unchanged) while restoring the exact defect the diff sets out to fix — with the newest run still in flight, `completed` is empty and `@claude rerun` re-runs nothing. The pagination/per_page part of the change is therefore unpinned while the test's title claims the copies are pinned.

samples.summary: set-state's gatherSignals rewiring to the scoped endpoint + ciConclusion is covered only by a source grep
samples.evidence: gatherSignals now calls `/actions/workflows/${CI_WORKFLOW_FILE}/runs` and `ciConclusion(runs)` instead of name-filtering and sorting by created_at. set-state.test.mjs (read in full, lines 1-120) imports only the pure helpers (STATES, computeLabelSet, deriveState, ...) and never exercises gatherSignals with a `gh` stub. The only coverage is the string assertion in checks.test.mjs:537-549 that the URL literal appears in the source. So a wiring mistake here (e.g. passing `data` instead of `data.workflow_runs`, or forgetting `|| []`) would ship green; impact is contained to a mislabelled lifecycle state.

samples.summary: Gate 1b's pagination and malformed-response refusals are untested
samples.evidence: branchEditsCiDefinition (mark-ready.mjs:181-195) has three uncovered paths: the multi-page loop (a page of exactly 100 files continues to page 2), the `>1000 changed files` throw at line 194, and the `unexpected response from the PR files endpoint` throw at line 184. The stub in mark-ready.test.mjs serves cfg.files on page 1 and `[]` thereafter, and every fixture has 1 file, so the loop always returns at `files.length < 100`. Only the forced-failure case (`fail: ["api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/7/files"]`) is exercised. A regression that read only page 1, or treated a non-array as empty, would fail open on exactly the large/odd PRs the comment says must refuse.
searchedFor: read the gate-1b test block in the diff/mark-ready.test.mjs

samples.summary: newestRun's `id ?? 0` fallback (runs with no id) is never exercised
samples.evidence: `newestRun` defends against a missing `id` with `(r.id ?? 0)`, but every fixture in checks.test.mjs (ciConclusion at 496-517, ciRunToRerun at 555-575, and the mirror fixtures at 603-610) supplies an integer id. The inline workflow mirror uses a bare `r.id > n.id`, so the two copies' behaviour on an id-less run is asserted nowhere. Impact is negligible in practice (the API always returns ids), which is why this is a nit rather than a gap.

samples.summary: The `trigger-shape` canary and its test exist only inside an unapplied .patch file, so neither runs
samples.evidence: The new docs/tasks/active/*.patch contains both a `trigger-shape` job for agent-review-panel.yml and a checks.test.mjs hunk asserting it. Neither is applied: the working-tree checks.test.mjs (read in full) has no `trigger-shape` assertion, and lines 456-458 are the blank gap where the hunk would land. That means the canary the patch's prose describes as the safety net for the three new `path` gates contributes zero coverage on this branch. Flagging only the coverage consequence — whether shipping the change as an inert patch is acceptable is the correctness/design lens's call.

verdict.reason: The `workflow_run.path` gate at .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:52-56 (a `contents: write` workflow, permissions at line 25) has no test. The only clause-evaluating test, scripts/agent/checks.test.mjs:128-219, explicitly reads agent-review-panel.yml (line 130), extracts its `gate:` if (line 169), and asserts pwn.yml refusal (206-214) — panel only. I searched repo-wide over *.mjs for both the literal `workflow_run.path` and the escaped-regex spelling `workflow_run\.path` that a naive grep misses; the only hits are checks.mjs:59 (comment) and checks.test.mjs:181 (the panel test's toJs rewrite). Other readers of agent-iterate-ci.yml assert unrelated literals: loop-status.test.mjs:327-333 (CI_PAGED_LATCH) and :335-356 (author allow-lists). scripts/test/agent-workflow-guards.test.mjs iterates every agent-*.yml (39-41) but only checks GH_REPO (48-63), workspace-code ordering (65-122) and agent-tools staging (124-193) — it never inspects a job `if:`. checks.test.mjs:443-454 and 520-553 pin CI_WORKFLOW_PATH/FILE inside mark-ready.mjs/set-state.mjs, and mark-ready.test.mjs:211-257 covers the API-scoping defence — different mechanism, different file, neither would fail if the YAML clause were deleted. Deleting the clause leaves the suite green, so a guard against a forged "CI"-named run driving the write-scoped fixer can regress silently: major under the missing-test branch of this lens.

Real fake/missing coverage over a user-invoked path that would silently no-op; no refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: Gate 1b's pagination is never exercised — the stub cannot even express a second page, so a reader that only ever looks at page 1 passes the whole suite
finding.evidence: `branchEditsCiDefinition` (mark-ready.mjs:181-195) loops up to 10 pages, continues while `files.length === 100`, and throws (fail-closed) past 1000 files. The stub's files branch is `page === 1 ? cfg.files || [] : []` (mark-ready.test.mjs:79-83), and every fixture in the new gate-1b test (lines 269-298) supplies 1-item single pages, so `files.length < 100` returns on page 1 in every run. Nothing asserts that a workflow edit appearing only on page 2+ is caught, and nothing asserts the >1000-file `throw` reaches the fail-closed exit-1 path. Delete the loop and keep only page 1, or invert the `< 100` continuation, and all tests still pass — while an `agent:managed` PR with >100 changed files that guts `.github/workflows/ci.yml` would auto-promote on its own gutted CI run, which is exactly the attack gate 1b is advertised to close. Searched mark-ready.test.mjs for `page=`, `per_page`, `1000 changed files` (one hit, in the stub itself).

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. mark-ready.mjs:181-195 (`branchEditsCiDefinition`) is new code — no such function or "gate 1b" exists in .trusted/scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs — and it paginates pulls/{n}/files up to 10 pages, continuing while files.length === 100 and throwing a fail-closed error past 1000 files. The gh stub cannot express that: mark-ready.test.mjs:79-83 serves `page === 1 ? cfg.files || [] : []`, so page 2+ is unconditionally empty. Every fixture supplies a 1-element array (okConfig at line 113; the gate-1b cases at 269-298, the rename at 284, the ordinary PR at 296), so files.length < 100 always returns on page 1 — the loop never iterates and the >1000-file throw at line 194 is never reached. The only fail-closed coverage (lines 290-293) comes from forcing the gh call to fail, exercising the catch in ranBaseCiDefinition (197-208) but not the refusal-on-oversize path. I searched beyond the reviewer's stated queries: repo-wide grep for branchEditsCiDefinition / CI_DEFINING_PREFIXES / previous_filename / "cannot rule out a workflow edit" (only the source, its test, and .agent-review artifacts), glob **/mark-ready* (only source + test + .trusted baselines), and grep page=|per_page|paginate across all *.test.mjs (no other test touches this endpoint). The loop is inline and private, so no indirect helper test can cover it. Result: removing pagination or inverting the `< 100` continuation keeps the suite green while a >100-file agent:managed PR that guts .github/workflows/ci.yml would auto-promote on its own gutted run — a new guard whose failure silently weakens promotion, i.e. a major missing-test gap in this lens's lane.
